To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the application of heat and BES + chloroform to suppress H2 consumption caused changes in the macro and microstructure of anaerobic sludge that were incompatible with high‐rate anaerobic reactors.

(i) heat treatment of granular sludges is not an appropriate method for the removal of H2‐con­suming bacteria, because it causes severe damage to granules; (ii) the BES treatment, when applied in the form of pulses, allows the removal of HSCB from granular sludge with minimal impact on its structural integrity and (iii) the combination of BES and chloroform treatments is not an appropriate approach for H2‐consumption removal because

the application of chemical treatments to suppress H2 consumers caused changes in granules structure and bacterial community that are incompatible with the operation and stability of high‐rate bioreactors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new methods for the control of the microbial activity of the granular sludge in high‐rate reactors for the treatment of wastewaters containing organic substrates.
the use of chemical and thermal treatments to control the activity of hydrogen consuming microorganisms in granular sludge used in high‐rate anaerobic processes.
the development of new strategies to control hydrogen‐consuming bacteria in anaerobic granular sludge and to increase the efficiency of anaerobic digestion of organic wastes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of BES +Chloroform and BES alone as strategies for hydrogen‐consuming bacteria control, can affect the macrostructure of granular anaerobic sludge, but only BES +chloroform caused significant microstructure changes.

the application of the BES strategy to the anaerobic granular sludge of a mesophilic EGSB reactor fed with synthetic sugar based wastewater was able to control the activity of H2‐consumers and to increase the hydrogen production rate to 1,000–700 ± 100 mL H2 L−1 day−1, without affecting the structure of the granules.

the use of BES to suppress hydrogen‐consumption is not a good strategy to improve H2 production in anaerobic reactors treating wastewater with high concentrations of readily biodegradable COD, as it can lead to granule disintegration and to a decrease in reactor efficiency.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, methods to suppress H2 consuming bacteria, such as heat and BES, have different effects on the structure of granular sludges.

the use of chemicals to suppress hydrogen‐producing bacteria in anaerobic granular sludge is a feasible strategy to improve the hydrogen production rate, but the granules structure is affected and it is necessary to monitor the microbiology and the granules structure.

the treatment of anaerobic sludge with heat or chemicals to suppress hydrogen‐producing microorganisms can cause structural changes in the sludge, which are detrimental for the operation of high rate anaerobic reactors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the strategies to suppress H2 consumers can cause changes in granules structure and microbial community, which can be in compatible with the operation of a high‐rate reactor, such as EGSB.

the use of chemical agents to suppress H2 consumers in anaerobic granular sludge can have a significant impact on the structure of the granules, which can affect the performance of high‐rate anaerobic reactors.

, the methods applied to suppress hydrogen consuming microorganisms can cause significant changes in the macro and microstructure of anaerobic sludge, which may be incompatible with the high‐rate operation of reactors.
